title: arXiv Mathematics daily notable papers — 20 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred shortlist, not a measured readership ranking; citation and independent-attention evidence is limited for papers this recent, so ordering reflects mathematical claims and scope rather than popularity.

sections.title: Amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves and applications
sections.abstract: The authors prove amplitude-dependent wave-envelope estimates for moment curves in arbitrary dimensions and use them to establish sharp small-cap decoupling inequalities for dimensions n≥4, resolving the Demeter–Guth–Wang exponential-sum conjecture in all dimensions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove amplitude-dependent wave-envelope estimates for moment curves and derive sharp small-cap decoupling for the moment curve in every dimension n≥4.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fourier restriction/decoupling for moment curves; the new sharp small-cap conclusion is for dimensions n≥4 and uses prior sharp square-function estimates by Maldague and Guth–Maldague.
sections.unique_caveat: The result concerns the moment curve, not general manifolds; the paper builds on those prior square-function estimates, and this summary has not independently checked the proof.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract claims sharp small-cap decoupling in every dimension n≥4 and completion of a named conjecture on exponential sums; this is a specific consequential result signal, not an attention metric.

sections.title: Sharp topological overlap in every dimension
sections.abstract: The author determines the asymptotic topological and affine overlap constants for maps of high-dimensional simplices into R^d, obtaining the same exact value in every dimension.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves c_d^top = c_d^aff = (d+1)!/(d+1)^(d+1) for every integer d≥1, confirming the conjectured affine value and matching it with the topological constant.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: As n→∞, for continuous or affine maps from the n-simplex to R^d, some point lies in the images of at least (c−o(1)) binom(n+1,d+1) of the d-faces.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract says the proof was found by GPT-6 Astra following the author's directions; it remains a preprint claim and has not been independently or formally verified here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives an exact all-dimensional constant and confirms the Bukh–Matoušek–Nivasch conjecture; its combinatorics/computational-geometry cross-listing corroborates scope, while no popularity claim is made.

sections.title: Hypergraph Hajnal-Szemerédi
sections.abstract: The authors improve the minimum-codegree sufficient condition for a perfect clique-factor in uniform hypergraphs, bringing it closer to the known codegree Turán lower bound.
sections.claimed_result: For each r≥3 there is c>0 such that for q>r and sufficiently large n divisible by q, codegree at least (1−c log^{1−1/(r−1)}(q)/q^(r−1))n guarantees a K_q^r-factor.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: G is an r-uniform hypergraph; the theorem assumes r≥3, q>r, q|n, and sufficiently large n. The bound is sufficient, not asserted to be exact.
sections.unique_caveat: The exact threshold remains open: the paper says its upper and lower bounds differ by a factor of order log^(1/(r−1))q; its suggested matching threshold is conjectural, not proved here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors give a concrete improvement to a long-standing general threshold problem and connect it to the known Turán obstruction; the paper also reports a fractional-threshold result and an independent-set lemma.

sections.title: A proof of Casselman's comparison conjecture
sections.abstract: The paper compares nilradical homology and related derived functors for the Harish–Chandra module of a representation and its smooth globalization.
sections.claimed_result: For a real linear reductive group, standard parabolic Q=LU, Casselman–Wallach representation π, and every i≥0, the inclusion of K-finite vectors induces a topological L-equivariant isomorphism between the globalization of H_i(u,π_K) and H_i(u,π); the authors also prove stated Tor/Ext comparisons for augmentation quotients.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Real linear reductive groups, standard parabolic subgroups, Casselman–Wallach representations, and associated Lie-algebra homology/cohomology and topological modules.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem has this specified real-group and smooth-globalization scope; it does not by itself settle every comparison problem for other canonical globalizations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors claim a proof of a named comparison conjecture across standard parabolics, with additional Tor/Ext and closed-image statements; the introduction identifies the broader conjectural context.

sections.title: On Romik's rationality conjectures for critical percolation
sections.abstract: For nested boundary-connection events in the critical-percolation O(1) loop model, the authors derive Pfaffian formulas and rationality in the cylinder and half-plane limits.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show that probabilities of k nested arches are rational functions of cylinder circumference for N>k and rational in the half-plane limit, establishing key aspects of Romik's conjectures.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Completely packed O(1) loops representing critical square-lattice bond percolation; fixed k nested-arch events on a semi-infinite cylinder of circumference 2N, with N>k, and the infinite-circumference half-plane limit.
sections.unique_caveat: The proof covers nested-arch events, not all boundary submatchings; the predicted denominator and numerator structure, dyadic rationality, and boundary case N=k remain unresolved in the paper.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result is cross-listed across probability, mathematical physics, and combinatorics and proves a precise part of a named conjecture using an explicit bridge through plane partitions, dimers, and Pfaffians.

sections.title: The existence of generalized Steiner systems
sections.abstract: The authors prove eventual existence of generalized q-ary Steiner systems at the Johnson-type bound for fixed parameters whenever the necessary divisibility conditions hold.
sections.claimed_result: For fixed q≥3 and w>t≥1, the authors prove a GS(t,w,n,q) exists for every sufficiently large n satisfying the stated divisibility conditions; distinct codeword supports can be chosen to intersect in at most t coordinates.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fixed integer parameters q≥3 and w>t≥1; n is sufficiently large and satisfies binom(w−i,t−i) | (q−1)^(t−i) binom(n−i,t−i) for each 0≤i<t.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract gives an eventual-existence theorem, not an explicit effective threshold for n or a practical construction algorithm.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract explicitly answers an existence question posed after a 2025 asymptotic result, upgrading asymptotic attainment to exact attainment for all sufficiently large admissible lengths.

sections.title: Dynamical edge universality and the Airy$_β$ line ensemble
sections.abstract: The authors prove convergence of rescaled edge trajectories to the Airy_β line ensemble for three families of interacting-particle systems from general non-equilibrium initial data under a regular-edge condition.
sections.claimed_result: For each fixed k, after the stated edge and time rescalings, the top k particle trajectories converge jointly in distribution to the top k curves of the Airy_β line ensemble.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: β-Dyson Brownian motion with analytic potential, weighted β-corners processes, and a class of discrete-time Markov chains; general non-equilibrium initial data and a regular square-root limiting-density edge.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is limited to the three model classes and regular square-root edges described; it does not assert universality at singular edges or for arbitrary interacting systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It treats three model families and every β>0, and is cross-listed in probability and mathematical physics; the abstract states a multi-time convergence claim rather than a single-time limit.

sections.title: Proof of Stanley's Conjecture on the Leading Ehrhart Coefficients of the Birkhoff Polytope
sections.abstract: For each fixed nonnegative k, the authors establish the asymptotic ratio of the coefficient c(n,k) to the leading Ehrhart coefficient of the n×n Birkhoff polytope, confirming Stanley's conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove c(n,k)/c(n,0) ~ n^(3k)/(2^k k!) as n→∞ for every fixed nonnegative integer k.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Ehrhart polynomial of the n×n Birkhoff polytope; k is fixed while n tends to infinity.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a fixed-k asymptotic statement, not an exact formula for finite n or a result uniform over growing k.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A precise conjecture confirmation with an explicit asymptotic formula makes this a checkable result signal rather than a title-only claim.

sections.title: The rational points of the non-split Cartan modular curve of level 121
sections.abstract: The author determines all rational points on the genus-511 level-121 non-split Cartan modular curve and relates this case to Galois images of non-CM elliptic curves over Q.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims that X_ns^+(121) has exactly seven rational points, all CM; together with the cited theorem of Rouse, Sutherland, and Zureick-Brown, this determines the 11-adic Galois images for non-CM elliptic curves over Q.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Rational points on the normalizer of a non-split Cartan modular curve at level 121, of genus 511; the Galois-image consequence is for non-CM elliptic curves over Q.
sections.unique_caveat: The result resolves the level-121 case only; it relies on specialized quadratic-Chabauty and Hecke-intersection arguments and does not classify all levels.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper cross-lists number theory and algebraic geometry and reports an exact rational-point classification for a high-genus curve, addressing a specified level case of a published conjecture.

sections.title: Infinitely Many Plasma Echo Cascades and Sobolev Norm Divergence at the Gevrey-3 Threshold
sections.abstract: The author constructs a global confined Vlasov–Poisson solution with infinitely many nonlinear plasma-echo cascades, producing Sobolev norm divergence despite decay of macroscopic fields.
sections.claimed_result: Near a fixed homogeneous Penrose-stable equilibrium, for every sufficiently small ε, the author constructs a real, neutral global solution with nonnegative distribution, initial size O(ε) in Gevrey-3 radius λ₀≈ε^(1/3), and ||f(t)||_{H^1000_{z,v}}→∞ as t→∞, although the kinetic profile scatters in a lower Sobolev topology and density and electric field decay.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Confined Vlasov–Poisson system near a fixed homogeneous Penrose-stable equilibrium; small perturbations at the amplitude-dependent Gevrey-3 radius specified in the abstract.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a constructed solution in a particular confined model and norm; it does not establish the same instability for general equilibria or Vlasov–Poisson settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract describes a constructed instability at a stated critical regularity scale, while also specifying scattering and field decay, making the contrast mathematically concrete.

sections.title: Permanence and 144-periodicity of $x_{153,3}$ in the stable stems at the prime three
sections.abstract: The author shows that a specified class in the 3-primary Adams–Novikov spectral sequence survives and generates a period-144 family in stable homotopy, answering a question of Carrick and Davies.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves permanence of x_{153,3} and the existence of a period-144 family, with iterates detected nontrivially at height two.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The 3-primary Adams–Novikov spectral sequence of the sphere; the class is in stable degree 153 and filtration 3.
sections.unique_caveat: This establishes a family from one specified class at the prime three; it does not imply periodicity for other classes or primes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result directly answers both parts of a named question and identifies a periodic family, a concrete signal within algebraic topology rather than evidence of broad attention.
